correctness.rationale: PASS: exact trihedral formula yields endpoint half-angle tangents bc/[(a+sqrt(a²+b²))(sqrt(a²+b²)+sqrt(a²+b²+c²))] and reversed for opposite endpoint; two middle solid angles equal atan(c/b) and atan(a/b). Holding b and a²+c² fixed, one endpoint decreases and the other increases as a passes c, so their minimum is strictly maximized at a=c. Then t=b/a gives symmetric endpoint F(t)=t/[(1+sqrt(1+t²))(sqrt(1+t²)+sqrt(2+t²))] with F'/F=(sqrt(t²+2)-t²)/[t sqrt(t²+1) sqrt(t²+2)], positive below sqrt2 and negative above. Thus unique upper bound 2atan(√2/(5+3√3)); at a=c=1,b=√2 both middle angles exceed the two matching endpoints, so it is the actual four-vertex maximin. Independent determinant geometry tests on 4000 arbitrary triples corroborated the value 0.2756427992162654 sr. Scope excludes degenerate shapes and general tetrahedra.
